_meta.description: Period- and region-scoped historical given-name variants (diminutives, familiar forms, and scribal abbreviations) mapped to their formal forms. Drives auto-expansion in fulltext_search (Lucene OR groups) and image_transcribe (VLM natural-language prompt). record_search and external sites already expand — see issue #1868. English only in this file; the Latin/cognate cross-language need is deliberately OUT OF SCOPE for #1868 (see `out_of_scope` below).
_meta.shape: per language -> per formal name -> { period, region, source, variants: [ { form, attested, source? } ] }. `attested` is per-VARIANT (not per formal name) so the measured/untested split is preserved exactly: only a variant with committed measured evidence is `attested: true`.
_meta.attested_note: Exactly three variant->formal pairs carry measured evidence: Betty->Elizabeth, Peggy->Margaret, Polly->Mary (membership test 8/8 over three name families, 2026-08-08). Every other variant is untested (attested: false) — present because it appears in the cited in-repo prose table, not because its reach was measured.
_meta.period_region_note: `period` ("1600-1900") and `region` ("England and Anglophone North America") are FILE-WIDE SCOPE DEFAULTS stamped identically on every formal-name entry — they describe the collection's intended coverage window, not a per-name or per-variant measurement, and no entry's tag was individually dated or localized. Period-appropriateness is a separate axis from `attested` (measured search-reach): a variant can be in-window but untested, or attested but modern. Some seeded variants are modern-only forms that fall OUTSIDE the 1600-1900 window despite inheriting the default tag — Liam (William), Lisa (Elizabeth), Chuck and Carl (Charles), Hank (Henry), Rick (Richard) — kept because they appear in the cited seed table; treat the entry-level period as an upper-bound scope statement, not a claim that every listed variant was in use across the whole window.
_meta.coverage_note: Coverage is uneven by source, not by omission. Four entries — Thomas, Samuel, Benjamin, George — come ONLY from the scribal-abbreviation seed table (search-strategies.md:56-71) and do not appear in the nicknames table (name-search-mechanics.md:202-219). They therefore ship only their sourced abbreviations (Thomas: Thos/Thos./Tho.; Samuel: Saml/Saml./Sam.; Benjamin: Benj/Benj./Benjm.; George: Geo/Geo.) and NO bare diminutives. The common diminutives for these names — Tom/Tommy (Thomas), Sam/Sammy (Samuel), Ben/Benny (Benjamin), Georgie (George) — were deliberately NOT added: they appear in neither seed table, and adding them would invent a source, which the `sourcing` rule forbids. Samuel is the sharpest case: `Sam.` (with the trailing period) is the sourced scribal abbreviation from search-strategies.md:65, while the bare given name `Sam` is intentionally NOT promoted because no seed row attests it. A consumer should read these four as abbreviation-only until a nicknames source is available for them.
_meta.sourcing: Every entry traces to an in-repo file:line. No source is invented.
_meta.out_of_scope: Cross-language name forms — the inline cognates in the seed tables (Hans/Honza for John, Diego for James, Paco/Pepe for Francis/Joseph) and the Latin/Spanish/German block at search-strategies.md:76-83 (Joannes<->John, Iacobus<->James, Catalina<->Catherine, Wilhelm<->William, etc.) — are deliberately excluded. They are a different substitution mechanism (cross-language cognate / ecclesiastical register-form equivalence, formal<->formal across languages), not within-language diminutive expansion, and #1868 was scoped English-only on 2026-08-24 over one combined name-form table to keep issue #607's expansion contract to a single kind of substitution. Not tracked by a separate issue yet. Note on Pepe: the seed table tags "(Spanish)" on Pepe only on the Joseph row (name-search-mechanics.md:218), not on the Francis row (:217), where Pepe also appears untagged; Pepe is nonetheless excluded from BOTH Francis and Joseph as a cross-language form. Applying the source's row-local tagging mechanically would wrongly retain the untagged Pepe on Francis — the exclusion here rests on the form being Spanish (established one row down), not on a tag present on the Francis row.
_meta.seed_inclusion_note: Source inclusion and mechanism classification are SEPARATE axes, and inclusion is decided first. A form ships if and only if it is present verbatim in an English seed table; its linguistic classification does not gate that inclusion. As a result, a few retained forms would, by the mechanism described in `out_of_scope`, otherwise read as out-of-scope: Greta and Rita (Margaret) and Trina (Catherine) are cross-language/cognate forms, and Carl (Charles) is a distinct Germanic name rather than an English diminutive of Charles. They are kept because they appear UNTAGGED in the English nicknames seed rows (name-search-mechanics.md), not because they pass the within-language diminutive test — removing them would edit the seed, which this file does not do (see `Didn't change` in the PR). The `out_of_scope` exclusion is therefore narrow: it removes only the forms the seed itself tags as foreign (Hans/Honza/Diego/Paco/Pepe) and the separate cross-language block at search-strategies.md:76-83; it does NOT retroactively strip untagged forms already present in the English seed. So the exclusion rule reads: exclude source-tagged foreign forms and the cross-language block; retain everything else the English seed lists verbatim, classification notwithstanding.
